questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: For me it was a mix of many aspect being trying new ways of learning from a completely different perspective, improving my english skills, opens some other career option and lastly to meet new people and improve as a person living on my own on the other side of the world.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the destination was an english speaking country and that it had an interesting university with units that I found exciting and with a focus on climate and sustainability.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been the best experience in my life. Both searching and trying out new units, but also for me personal. I have developed a lot.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy and the abroad university was really good in assisting whenever there was a problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed assistance in some unit changes and it was a bit difficult to get in touch with the person in charge from my home university, which ment it took some weeks for it to be settled. When I got in touch was it really good assistance and the problem was solved fast with really good help from the abroad university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was good with a long orientation upon arrival as it made it easy to meet new people and get good a feeling of the university, which just made it an easy and comfortable start.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me and my friend, but many I meet down here had a really difficult time finding a place to live more permanently. I found mine through a facebook website called Fairyfloss.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should find it before coming to Melbourne. It is not as easy to find living off campus upon arrival as some may say and it takes a lot of energy in the beginning running around trying to find something or living in a hostel for a long period.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If I should rate my own experience it would be a 5, but I meet so many people in Melbourne who had a really difficult time finding, why I give it 4.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Of course it takes some time, but I did not feel that any of it was unnecessary.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I started by choosing my wished units, which was easy in my case as all my unit was of free choice, I did not have any mandatory units I needed to take. Then on mail I received which units I got and a link for me to change time for the different units.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There website helped as i was really informative and it was easy to get all the information needing when choosing units.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, so really successful. It was also easy to choose when to take the classes. If it was a big class I was able to wish for a specific time, so I could maximize my time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read carefully about your desired units and how they are structured as it is quite different from home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did not feel that the courses is of the same level as my home university. It could be because I tried some other directions than the one I read at home, but the units was easier than the ones I take home. The fact that attendance is a part of your grade make some point really easy to get.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is completely different. You are being graded on many different assignments, quizzes, discussion, attendance and so on. In some ways I liked it a lot because in some part you are stronger than others. Also the lectures it self was mostly recorded and the when you came to school it was for workshops, tutorials or guest lectures. The hours you spent in schools is way less than at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Designing for sustainability, Economics of climate change and Climate change communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both Economics of climate change and Climate change communication as they spoke well with each other and I feel like I learned some really good tools and got an insight I did not have before.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not really experience any unexpected costs other than the whole experience was more expensive than I first thought. But that is mostly because I did many trips i weekends and semester breaks to experience the country, which I really would recommend.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in the supermarket is more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offer everything you desire.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the lest orientation week which was really nice. Else there is every sport you can think of, a gym, a spa, clubs for everything, surf trips and I could go on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf-trips and just stay at the library as there are always different activities out on the court for free attendance.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mornington Peninsula is a really nice place for wine tasting, see kangaroos, stay at the beach and just get out of the big city. Also great ocean road is a must, but there you need a full weekend. For holidays Cairns is a good place in the winter time and you feel that Melbourne is cold and it is summer in Copenhagen. Byron bay is a really nice surf town with a chill vibe. Uluru is absolutely amazing and stunning and is a must hen you come to Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy I would say as everyone speak english and Melbourne is a metropol for all cultures so you feel very welcome.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is difficult to meet local students in Melbourne as there are a lot coming from around the world, but engage in class discussion and be upon when people walk by and start a conversation because you never know who your next friend is.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any cultural differences challenging as Melbourne is somehow similar to Copenhagen is many ways.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open people are! Everyone wants to share their story and give tips for anything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the orientation week as you will meet the people you will spent the most of your time with there.
Read about the assessments of your units so your school work is spread out and you do not end up having weekly assignments in every unit.
Stay at the library and join some of the free events and activities there are throughout the day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can choose between all units, then try something a little bit different from what you study at home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My personal growth being own my own on the other side of the world in an english speaking country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from home, but it was also the best part.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
